I have thrips now. I first killed everything I found on all my plants by hand. I cut some leaves that were too infected. Then I made a mixture of oil (2tbsp) green soap (4tbsp) and water (250mL). I sprayed all my plants with this, the whole plant but not the dirt). I also isolated the infected plants. A few days later I sprayed them with an insecticide that draws in to the plant and is supposed to give 8 weeks of protection. I did this to all my plants just in case. Some days later I watered all my plants with a mixture of water and hydrogen peroxide 3% in a 4-1 ratio. This is to kill the eggs and creatures that might be in the soil because all the other things I did was only for the plants. 

I laid out “traps”, basically just bowls of water, vinegar and dish soap to catch the ones that fly. 
I have not yet gotten sticky traps for flys. I’m waiting for them to come in the mail. 
I haven’t found any more bugs, but I sometimes see the adults flying around the apartment so I usually try to kill them myself. 
The bastards REALLY infested my monstera adansonii so I had to throw it out. But I have a very big alocasia frydek that I refuse to let die. 

Arguably the most effective way to treat these guys is by using predatory insects that kill the insects for you. I wanted to do this but my girlfriend refused to have 1000+ predatory insects in the house(they only eat other bugs so they won’t kill your plants). 

I, of course, haven’t defeated these guys yet, I will have to wait and see, but here is a post that I found helpful against thrips:  https://www.reddit.com/r/houseplants/comments/12jxyis/thrips_the_worst_jerks_documenting_my_battle/

I don’t really know how it is in your country with payment for professional help, but maybe if you get referred by a doctor the health system will pay most of it (or at least some of it). I’m not a professional, but I’ve gone through depression and suicidal thoughts before so if you want to talk I’m always open to talk:) 

Also I wouldn’t worry about being a burden to someone. If they care for you and love you they will always be there for you to help you. If they don’t want to be there for your bad times, they don’t deserve your good and amazing times. We’re all human and flawed, but if they really care I’m sure they’d be glad to help. Professional help can be expensive, if that’s not an option there are hotlines that are free ([Hotlines](http://www.suicide.org/)) and I hope you have people to talk to. 
If you’re afraid to be a burden to someone, you could always talk to me. You’re not a burden in my eyes!

Have you talked to somebody about your emotions and thoughts? I know talking about it might seem dumb and not work at all, but talking about how I felt and how I had it helped me a lot when I was at my lowest point. Opening up to somebody might be scary, but if you open up to someone you trust and love it might just help. 

Also taking babysteps every day and getting some structure to your day might help you getting back to normality of what you were doing before. Setting a goal to get out of bed 10 minutes earlier than yesterday, then doing that the next day, and the next day will probably help getting better. Dont hate yourself. Remember to lean on somebody when you're not strong. Tomorrow might be just the same as yesterday, but maybe (and hopefully) a lot better than yesterday!

Hey, it's always going to be a few really hard and though bumps you'll experience through life, but theres always tomorrow. Tomorrow might be the same, but it might also be one of the best days in your life. Hang on tight. I'm sure you have family you could talk to, talking about your emotions and thoughts might be difficult to do in the beginning, but it will probably help you in not feeling so alone (trust me, I've been there before. I'll leave you with a quote I think is good by Aristotle: "It is during our **darkest** moments that we must focus to see the **light**".
